meta_title: QuickSnap: free screenshot and annotation tool for macOS
meta_description: QuickSnap is a free, lightweight screenshot and annotation app for macOS, written in Rust. Capture, mark up, blur, save or copy. No accounts, no uploads, no telemetry.
og_description: Capture, mark up, save or copy. A tiny native menu-bar app written in Rust. No accounts, no uploads, no telemetry.
og_image_alt: QuickSnap home screen with its capture actions
hero_tagline_strong: Take a screenshot, mark it up, save or copy it.
hero_tagline_rest: A tiny, native menu-bar app for macOS, written in Rust.
hero_alt: QuickSnap home screen with six capture actions: area, full screen, full screen after 10 seconds, frozen area, record video and open from clipboard
promise_2_text: Your pixels stay on your Mac
features_eyebrow: Everything you need, nothing you don't
features_title: From hotkey to clipboard in a couple of seconds
features_lead: Press a shortcut, drag over what matters, add an arrow, and it's ready to paste into a chat, a ticket or a document.
f1_text: Selected area, frozen area (the screen freezes while you choose), full screen, or full screen after a 10-second delay. Click to grab a single window or a whole display, on any connected screen.
f2_text: Full-screen recording to a .mov file, with the pointer and your clicks shown.
f3_text: Arrows, rectangles, ellipses, lines, freehand pen, text and callouts. Move and resize every item afterwards.
f4_text: Blur passwords, email addresses and faces. Crop, rotate and resize without leaving the editor.
f5_text: A light shadow on a transparent PNG, so a screenshot with a white background still stands out once pasted into an email.
f6_text: No Dock icon. Close the window and it keeps running, with every command in the menu-bar icon too.
f7_text: Global shortcuts for every action, plus save folder, PNG or JPEG, and file-name templates.
f8_text: Up to 40 steps of undo and redo. Pinch, or [[cmd]] + scroll, to zoom around the pointer.
f9_text: After each capture: open the editor, save to a folder, copy to the clipboard, or open it in Preview.
editor_lead: A clean canvas with floating glass toolbars. Pick a tool, pick a colour, click and drag.
tool_shapes: arrows, rectangles, ellipses and lines, in any width
tool_blur: areas you can still move and resize
tool_zoom: pinch, [[cmd]] + scroll, or the zoom menu
editor_alt: QuickSnap annotation editor: a sample picture with a red rectangle, two arrows and text, the tool bar at the top and the colour palette at the bottom
prefs_lead: A see-through window with your desktop blurred behind it, a colour-gradient backdrop and no title bar. Tune it all in Preferences.
prefs_general_alt: Preferences, General tab: interface language, what happens after a screenshot, external editor and menu-bar options
prefs_general_cap: General: language, what happens after each capture, external editor
prefs_hotkeys_alt: Preferences, Hotkeys tab: a global shortcut field for each capture action
prefs_hotkeys_cap: Hotkeys: one global shortcut per action
prefs_appearance_alt: Preferences, Appearance tab: theme (automatic, light or dark) and capture overlay options
prefs_appearance_cap: Appearance: automatic, light or dark theme
langs_lead: Pick it from the home screen or from Preferences. Chinese, Japanese and Korean use macOS's own fonts.
step2_text: Open the DMG and drag QuickSnap into your Applications folder.
step3_text: The first time, go to [[mac:settings]] → [[mac:privacy]] and click [[mac:open_anyway]].
step4_text: Turn QuickSnap on in [[mac:privacy]] → [[mac:screen]], then reopen the app.
note_notarized: QuickSnap is not notarized by Apple yet. That is why macOS asks you to confirm the first time you open each version.
note_silicon: Release builds are for Apple Silicon Macs. On Intel Macs, build it from source with one command.
build_comment_1: build from source (needs Rust and the Xcode Command Line Tools)
final_lead: Free, small and private. Give it a try, and star the repository if it saves you some clicks.
footer_by: QuickSnap is made by Joan Galtés i Moreno.
footer_built: Built in Rust with [[egui]] and [[tinyskia]], with help from [[claude]].
banner_text: This page is also available in English.

guide_hero_link: First time? How to open QuickSnap on your Mac
guide_meta_title: How to open QuickSnap on your Mac
guide_meta_description: Step-by-step guide with pictures: how to open QuickSnap the first time on macOS, allow it in Privacy & Security and turn on screen recording.
guide_title: How to open QuickSnap the first time
guide_lead: QuickSnap is free and open source, but it is not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS asks you to confirm before opening it. It only takes a minute, and you only need to do it once per version.
guide_pictures_note: The pictures show macOS in English. On your Mac, look for the names in bold in each step.
guide_s1_text: Open QuickSnap.dmg from your Downloads folder and drag the QuickSnap icon onto the Applications folder.
guide_s1_alt: The QuickSnap disk window, with an arrow from the QuickSnap icon to the Applications folder
guide_s2_text: Open QuickSnap from the Applications folder. macOS says it could not verify the app. Click [[mac:done]]. Don’t click [[mac:trash]], or you will have to download QuickSnap again.
guide_s2_alt: The macOS warning “QuickSnap” Not Opened, with the Done button highlighted
guide_s3_text: Open [[mac:settings]] from the Apple menu, choose [[mac:privacy]] in the sidebar and scroll down to [[mac:security]]. Next to [[mac:blocked]], click [[mac:open_anyway]].
guide_s3_tip: Don’t see the button? It only appears for about an hour after step 2. Open QuickSnap again and come back here.
guide_s3_alt: The Security section of Privacy & Security, with the Open Anyway button highlighted
guide_s4_text: macOS asks one last time. Click [[mac:dlg_open_anyway]] and confirm with Touch ID or your password. QuickSnap opens and its icon appears in the menu bar.
guide_s4_alt: The macOS dialog Open “QuickSnap”?, with the Open Anyway button highlighted
guide_s5_text: The first time you take a screenshot, macOS asks for permission. In [[mac:settings]] → [[mac:privacy]] → [[mac:screen]], turn on QuickSnap. Then quit QuickSnap from its menu-bar icon and open it again.
guide_s5_alt: The Screen & System Audio Recording list, with QuickSnap turned on
guide_done_text: Press [[keys:5]] to capture an area. From now on, QuickSnap opens normally.
guide_update_text: macOS checks every new download, so after installing a new version you will need to repeat steps 2 to 4, and maybe turn on screen recording again. Your settings are kept.

guide_why_text: Apple checks (“notarizes”) apps from outside the App Store when their developer pays for a yearly Apple Developer membership. QuickSnap is a free personal project and is not notarized yet. Its source code is public on GitHub, so anyone can check what it does or build it themselves.
guide_help_text: Still stuck? Open an issue on GitHub and tell us what you see.
